key_insight: Ideal liquid crystal elastomers couple mesogen orientation with network deformation, enabling reversible actuation and finite deformation at nearly zero stress.
engineering_relevance: The theory provides a constitutive foundation for modeling soft actuators and predicting stretch-dependent mechanical responses in liquid crystal elastomers.
method: Connect anisotropic Gaussian-chain statistics to neo-classical continuum elasticity.
Relate stress-free ground states to spontaneous deformation and soft stripe-domain formation.
Use quasi-convex energy relaxation to classify three macroscopic response regimes in polydomain elastomers.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a theoretical review and three predicted polydomain response regimes, but reports no experimental dataset or quantitative validation.
watch_item: Ideal behavior assumes no memory of the crosslinking state; realistic predictions may require network nonideality, director-gradient elasticity, and temperature- and rate-dependent viscoelasticity.
paper_title: Elastic theory of ideal liquid crystal elastomers
